nodes.label: Random Traders
nodes.rationale: Zero-intelligence traders acting for real needs; buy/sell with equal probability; act as 'thermal bath' that stabilizes price; active with p=0.1; receive mined Bitcoins.

nodes.label: Chartists
nodes.rationale: Trend-following speculators; buy if relative price variation over window tau_i > Th=0.01, sell if < -Th; active with p=0.5; essential to reproduce fat tails and volatility clustering.

nodes.label: Order book / price clearing mechanism
nodes.rationale: Single global order book approximates the many independent Bitcoin exchanges since prices are public; buy orders sorted descending by limit price, sell ascending, ties by issue time; similar to Raberto et al. 2005.

nodes.label: Transaction price formation rules
nodes.rationale: Market vs limit: pT=min(bi,p) or max(sj,p); both market: pT=p(t); both limit: pT=(bi+sj)/2.

nodes.label: Buy and sell orders
nodes.rationale: Amount, residual amount, limit price, issue time, expiration time; no short selling.

nodes.label: Lognormal beta order-size factor (mean 0.25, sd 0.2)
nodes.rationale: Lognormal chosen for multiplicative, positive, percentage-balanced factor.

nodes.label: Limit price via Gaussian draw N(mu=1.02, sigma_i=K*sigma(Ti))
nodes.rationale: Random term models differing perception of value; follows Raberto et al. 2001.

nodes.label: Market order probability Plim (0.2 Random, 0.7 Chartist)
nodes.rationale: Conservative 20% for Random due to scarce liquidity; 70% for Chartists to follow trend at best price.

nodes.label: Order expiration time
nodes.rationale: Random traders: lognormal mean 3 sd 1 days; Chartists: end of same day.

nodes.label: Mining of new Bitcoins (not explicitly modelled)
nodes.rationale: New Bitcoins proportional to real daily increase assigned to random fraction of Random Traders proportional to holdings; Chartists excluded since speculation inconsistent with miner behavior.

nodes.label: New traders inflow from Blockchain unique addresses
nodes.rationale: Number of traders tracks 30-day moving average of unique addresses; new traders endowed only with cash; leaving traders sell all via market order.

nodes.label: Pareto / Zipf wealth distribution (alpha=1)
nodes.rationale: Built with power-law ranking property; new traders use alpha=0.6; realistic because financial power of traders varies hugely (Levy & Solomon 1997).

nodes.label: Model calibration (830 daily steps, 1/100 market scale)
nodes.rationale: Sized at 1/100 of real market to manage computational load; Jan 2012-Apr 2014; weekends included as Bitcoin trades every day.

nodes.label: Stylized facts of financial price series
Unit-root property
nodes.rationale: Price memory only via chartist threshold and volatility-based spread, too weak to break random walk.

nodes.label: Fat-tail phenomenon (excess kurtosis)
nodes.rationale: Due to Zipf wealth distribution affecting order sizes and Chartist herding.

nodes.label: Volatility clustering
nodes.rationale: Due to Chartist behavior and limit price spread tied to past volatility.

nodes.label: Autocorrelation of raw vs absolute returns
Trader total wealth w_i(t)=c_i(t)+b_i(t)p(t)
nodes.rationale: Random/Chartist wealth ratio stays roughly constant, so Chartist strategy is not winning.

nodes.label: Mean-reverting price toward cash/Bitcoin ratio
nodes.rationale: Explains why simulated spikes are lower than real; price rises because new traders bring more cash than mined Bitcoins.
